title: Nexus Fundamentals
description: Every new hire takes it: sign in and set up your phone, punch in and fix a missed punch, sign your Time Sheet, request time off and HR help, report problems with tickets and forms, and take your training. The first course of the Greens Storage Academy.
overview: Sign in, find your way around and set up Nexus on your phone
Punch in, take breaks, punch out and fix a missed punch
Read and sign your Time Sheet
Confirm your schedule and request time off
Use Ask HR, Reimbursements and Purchase Requests
Get help with tickets, Report a Problem and forms
Find people, borrow equipment, keep notes and take your training
teaches: Dashboard, Workday, Time Clock, Time Sheet, Time Off, Shifts, Team, Reimbursements, Help Center, Tickets, Forms, Item Management, Notes, Knowledge Base, Sidebar

questions.q: You reach Escondido 25 minutes before your shift and tap Punch In. Early Clock-In appears, and nobody asked you to start early. What do you tap?
questions.explanation: Not Yet cancels; punch in at your start time. Clock In Anyway records the punch and your manager is told, so use it only when your manager asked you to start early.

questions.q: You forgot to punch out yesterday. This morning a red bar says yesterday's shift is Missing. What do you do?
options: Tap Fix My Punch Out and ask for the real time
Punch in, then punch out right away to close it
Leave it; payroll fixes it at the end of the period
Ask a coworker to punch you out from their phone
questions.explanation: Fix My Punch Out takes you to your Time Sheet to ask for the real clock-out time with a reason. Punching in and out now creates a second, wrong shift.

questions.q: Your phone's location is turned off when you tap Punch In. Nexus still records the punch.
questions.explanation: True. A punch never waits for location and is never blocked by it. It is recorded as Location Off, and a Needs Attention bar offers Turn On or Skip.

questions.q: At 4:45 PM in the back RV row you tap Punch Out and see Your Punch Did Not Record: saved on this phone. What now?
options: Punch in and out again at the office
Ask your manager to delete the shift
Tap OK, Keep Trying and walk on
Tap Punch Out again until it works
questions.explanation: The punch is saved at 4:45 PM, the time you pressed it, and sends itself when signal returns. Punching again would create a wrong punch.

questions.q: You finish a shift on the shared office computer at Valley Center. What is the last thing you do in Nexus?
options: Lock the screen and leave it signed in
Turn on Dark Mode for the next person
Sign Out from your profile menu, which clears your data saved on it
questions.explanation: Sign Out ends your session and clears the copy of your data saved on that computer. A closed tab or a locked screen can leave the next person acting as you.

questions.q: A coworker says to check Tickets for the gate repair, but Tickets is not in your menu. What does that mean?
options: You do not have that module's grant
Your sign-in did not finish loading
Your tier is too low to raise tickets
questions.explanation: The desk side of Tickets is a grant. Without it you still raise and follow tickets in Help Center, which everyone has.

questions.q: You clicked Clear All in the bell and now need a ticket reply you cleared. Where is it?
options: In the yellow priority bar at the top of the screen
questions.explanation: Clear All moves updates to Closed, where they stay for 30 days and can be restored. Nothing you clear is gone right away.

questions.q: You can change your own bank details by clicking Edit under Contact & Emergency.
questions.explanation: False. Contact & Emergency covers your personal email, phone and emergency contact. Bank details, name, job and department go through Ask HR, Profile Change.

questions.q: Push to This Device will not turn on. You opened Nexus in Chrome on your iPhone. What fixes it?
options: Turn on Dark Mode under Appearance
Ask HR to switch push on for your account
Sign in with Partner Sign-In instead
Install from Safari (Share, Add to Home Screen), then open the icon
questions.explanation: An iPhone installs Nexus only from Safari (Share, Add to Home Screen), and push works only in the installed app.

questions.q: Tuesday, your Time Sheet shows Missing for Monday's clock-out. You left at 5:20 PM. What do you send?
options: A new punch in and out now, to close Monday
A Teams message to your manager with the time
Nothing; your manager fills it in at review
A request for 5:20 PM with a reason
questions.explanation: Click Missing and send a request with the real time and what happened. Your manager decides; a new punch would add a wrong shift.

questions.q: Your manager approved your Time Sheet, so that approval also counts as its signature.
questions.explanation: False. Your manager approves and never signs. Only you sign your Time Sheet, with Sign & Submit in Nexus Sign.

questions.q: A banner on My Schedule asks you to confirm next week's new schedule. Wednesday does not work for you. What do you do?
options: Request the day off as Sick
Confirm it, then talk to your manager about Wednesday
Leave it unconfirmed until it changes
Swap the shift with a teammate by text
questions.explanation: Confirm means I have seen it. Then raise the problem with your manager. An unconfirmed schedule just shows your manager you never looked.

questions.q: Your vacation day on 12/04/2026 was approved. On 12/05 your Time Sheet shows nothing for 12/04. What do you do?
options: Ask HR to punch the hours in for you
Punch in and out now for eight hours
Add it: Add on the day, Type Vacation, so the hours are paid
Wait; approved time off appears by itself
questions.explanation: Approved time off is not added for you. Click Add on the day and pick Vacation so the hours are paid.

questions.q: Your manager told you to buy printer paper with your own card. Where do you file it?
questions.explanation: You already paid, so you file a reimbursement with the receipt and the business purpose. A purchase request is for something the company has not bought yet.

questions.q: The site needs two padlocks for overlocks, and Item Management has none to borrow. What do you file?
options: A ticket to the IT department
questions.explanation: A purchase request asks the company to buy something it does not own. A reimbursement is only for something you already paid for.

questions.q: Your ticket about a dead light says Waiting for User. What does the team need?
questions.explanation: Waiting for User means the team is stuck until you answer. Waiting for Vendor is the status for an outside company.

questions.q: A borrowed dolly you handed back by hand stays on your record until the return is confirmed in Nexus.
questions.explanation: True. Until Start Return and Confirm Return are done, with a photo, the item is still yours on the record.

questions.q: You scored 76% on the final quiz and have two tries left. What is the best next step?
options: Click Try Again right away while it is fresh
Ask your manager to mark the course passed
Skip it and start the next course
Reread the lessons listed under Reread these, then Try Again
questions.explanation: The next try draws different questions, so rereading the lessons under Reread these before you try again is what moves the score.

questions.q: At Temecula a tenant asks whether their unit is paid up. Where do you look?
questions.explanation: Tenants, units and payments live in Cubby. Nexus is for your own work: time, requests, help and training.

questions.q: You see an outline shield beside the name of the person who approves your Time Sheet. What does it tell you?
options: They are on shift right now
questions.explanation: An outline shield marks an Administrator. A filled shield is a Super Administrator, and a small people icon a Manager.

questions.q: Two Employees at Murrieta have different menus: one sees Tasks and one does not. Why?
options: One works more hours each week than the other
One holds a grant, from a job role or an Access Group, the other does not
One signed in with Partner Sign-In
One has not finished their training yet
questions.explanation: Grants from a job role or an Access Group open extra modules on top of the tier, so menus differ between people of the same tier.

questions.q: Under a person's name, Nexus shows their tier, such as Manager or Administrator.
questions.explanation: False. Nexus shows the job title under a name. The tier is only a small mark beside the name, and Employees and Supervisors have none.

questions.q: You need a coworker's phone number fast. What is quickest from any screen?
options: Open Settings and find People & Access
Scroll the left menu down to Team, then Directory
Ask in the Teams chat for it
Press Ctrl+K and type their name
questions.explanation: Search Nexus (Ctrl+K or /) finds people from anywhere and opens their contact card.

questions.q: A screen in Nexus is new to you. Where is a guided walk-through of it?
options: Help Center, then Submit a Ticket
Search Nexus for the word tour
questions.explanation: Every screen has a tour under the ? Help panel. Help with This Page opens the written guide for the same screen.

questions.q: Weeks after your first sign-in, the policy notice appears again. Why?
options: The company published a new version of its policies
Your account was reset by IT overnight
You signed in from a different phone today
questions.explanation: The notice returns each time the company publishes a new version of its policies. Read it, tick the box and Accept & Continue.

questions.q: On your iPhone, where do you install Nexus from?
options: Safari, Share, Add to Home Screen
Chrome, then Profile, then the Install button
questions.explanation: An iPhone installs web apps only from Safari, by hand. The Install button in Profile is for Android in Chrome or Edge.

questions.q: Push to This Device is on, but a company-wide broadcast never reaches your phone. Why?
options: Your phone is too old for push
Push is off for your site
questions.explanation: Push carries the notices in your own bell. Company-wide broadcasts never push, so nothing is wrong with your setup.

questions.q: A form you send with no signal is saved on your phone and sends itself when signal returns.
questions.explanation: True. It shows Saved on This Phone and sends itself. Sending the same entry twice never creates two, so never redo it.

questions.q: Your Dashboard shows Signatures Needed: 1. What is waiting?
options: A shift for you to confirm this week
A document for you to sign
A ticket for you to answer
An item for you to return
questions.explanation: Signatures Needed counts documents waiting for your signature, such as an HR form or a Time Sheet. Click the tile to open it.

questions.q: A coworker read about new gate hours in an announcement; you never saw it. Why might that be?
options: Your bell is set to Mark All Read
You never added the Announcements widget
questions.explanation: Announcements reach your Dashboard only through the Announcements widget, which is not on Home by default. Add it with Customize, Add Widget.

questions.q: A yellow bar across the top says your Time Sheet is waiting for your signature. What do you do?
options: Dismiss it until payday comes around
Click Open and act on it
questions.explanation: The yellow priority bar means something is held up by you. Open goes straight to the item, and acting on it clears the bar.

questions.q: You click Mark All Read in the bell. What changes?
options: The red count clears; nothing is removed
Every notice moves to Closed for 30 days
Your toasts stop for the day
questions.explanation: Mark All Read only clears the count. Clear All is the one that moves updates to Closed for 30 days.

questions.q: Your last name is misspelled on your record. How do you get it fixed?
questions.explanation: Your name, job, department and bank details are part of your HR record, so HR changes them through Ask HR, Profile Change.

questions.q: HR sends your hiring packet forms. Where do they wait for your signature?
options: The Approvals tab, under Team Approvals
The Time Sheet tab, under Sign & Submit
questions.explanation: Nexus Sign documents wait at the top of the Workday Overview under Documents to Sign. Time Sheets are the exception: they are signed on the Time Sheet tab.

questions.q: A landlord wants to see a paystub. Where are your paystubs?
questions.explanation: Paystubs are a folder in My Documents. For proof of employment, Ask HR, Request a Letter is better than a paystub.

questions.q: Clicking outside the Ask HR panel closes it and keeps your draft.
questions.explanation: False. A click outside does not close the panel: it nudges it and lights up its close button. Close it with Close, Cancel or Escape.

questions.q: You tap Start Break. What does the Going on break box need from you?
options: A short reason, such as Lunch
Your location turned on and a photo of the site
questions.explanation: The break reason is required and posts to your team's Teams chat. The Resuming work note at End Break is the optional one.

questions.q: You punched in from the office computer. Your Time Sheet shows Approx. Location. Why?
options: A computer gives only a rough location, so no site name shows
You were away from every company location
questions.explanation: A computer usually gives only a rough location. Punch from your phone on site for a precise one that shows the site name.

questions.q: A Still on Break? notice reaches your bell. What does it usually mean?
options: You took a break that was too short
You forgot to press End Break
questions.explanation: A break left open about an hour brings Still on Break? Press End Break now and fix the time on your Time Sheet if it is wrong.

questions.q: An early punch is recorded, and your manager gets a notice about it.
questions.explanation: True. Nexus never blocks an early punch; Clock In Anyway records it and your manager is told. Start early only when asked.

questions.q: You are hourly at a California site and missed a meal break on Tuesday. The signing screen shows the break statement. What do you do?
options: Decline the whole Time Sheet in Nexus Sign
Report a Missed Break for Tuesday instead of signing
Sign it; the break is too small to matter
Sign it and email HR afterward
questions.explanation: Report a Missed Break, pick Tuesday and Meal, and send it back; your manager adds the premium pay. Never sign a statement that is not true.

questions.q: Who signs your Time Sheet?
questions.explanation: Only the employee signs. The manager approves and never signs, and nobody can sign for you.

questions.q: After your manager approved, you notice your Thursday 2:00 PM to 5:00 PM shift is missing. What do you do?
options: Sign it and fix Thursday next period
Sign it; your manager will catch it
Punch in and out for those hours now
Decline in Nexus Sign and say Thursday is missing
questions.explanation: Decline with what is wrong, or ask for a punch fix on Thursday. Either sends it back to your manager to correct before you sign.

questions.q: You asked for a missing clock-out. What does that day show until your approver decides?
questions.explanation: A change request shows Not Yet Approved on its day until your approver decides. You can still Cancel Request while it waits.

questions.q: Your Time Sheet shows 8:15 for Monday. How long did you work?
questions.explanation: Nexus shows hours as hours and minutes, never decimals, so 8:15 is eight hours and fifteen minutes.

questions.q: If HR changes your Time Sheet after you signed it, you are asked to sign the updated one.
questions.explanation: True. HR can correct a Time Sheet at any point, and you sign the updated one, or decline it with what is wrong.

questions.q: You were sick yesterday and could not request it in time. Yesterday is grayed out on the form. What do you click?
options: Add on the Time Sheet only
questions.explanation: Past dates are grayed out on Request Time Off; Request for a Past Date is how you ask for a day already gone.

questions.q: A teammate agreed to swap Saturday with you, and the request reads Waiting On Manager. Which shift do you work?
questions.explanation: A swap waits on the teammate, then a manager. Until the manager approves, the original shift stands.

questions.q: As an hourly employee, you are paid for a company holiday you do not work.
questions.explanation: False. For hourly staff a company holiday is a day off with no pay. Hours you do work on a holiday are paid as usual.

questions.q: You want your team to see only that you are out, not why. What do you tick?
options: Send it to HR instead of your manager
questions.explanation: Keep this confidential shows your team only that you are out. Your approver still sees the request.

questions.q: You have a question about your health benefits. Where do you send it?
options: A ticket to the HR desk
questions.explanation: Ask HR is the confidential HR desk: only you, the people you add and HR see the request.

questions.q: Your reimbursement comes back Sent Back. What do you do?
options: Read What to fix, then Fix and Resubmit the same claim
File a brand new claim with the same receipt
Ask HR to approve it anyway
Cancel it and pay it yourself
questions.explanation: Sent Back says what needs fixing. Change it and Fix and Resubmit the same claim; a second claim would duplicate it.

questions.q: You bought supplies today and the receipt is in your car. Can you file the claim now?
options: Only if your manager files it
Yes; add it later with Add Receipt
No; Nexus refuses a claim without a receipt attached
questions.explanation: You can send it now and use Add Receipt later. HR does not pay it until the receipt is attached.

questions.q: Your manager can read an Ask HR request you send, even if you do not add them.
questions.explanation: False. An Ask HR request is seen only by you, the people you add and HR.

questions.q: The front office light and the gate keypad both fail on the same morning. How many tickets do you raise?
questions.explanation: One problem per ticket: the two may go to different people, and each needs its own photo and status.

questions.q: Your ticket shows Resolved, but the gate still sticks. What do you click?
options: Confirm Resolution, then a new ticket
questions.explanation: Reopen works while a ticket is Resolved. Confirm Resolution only after you have checked the fix yourself.

questions.q: You scan the QR tag on Building C and Open Tickets already lists the same door. What does that tell you?
options: The tag is broken and needs replacing
You lack access to the place
questions.explanation: Open Tickets on a place lists what is already reported there, so you can follow it instead of filing a second one.

questions.q: You filled the site inspection at the back fence with no signal, and it shows Saved on This Phone. What next?
options: Take a screenshot and email it
Nothing; it sends itself when signal returns, or tap Sync Now
Fill it again at the office so it is not lost
questions.explanation: It sends itself when signal returns, and sending twice never creates two. Sync Now on the bar sends it right away.

questions.q: Your manager assigns you a laptop to keep. Is a photo required to accept it?
questions.explanation: Accepting an assigned item takes an optional photo. Handover, receipt and every return need one; a lost report needs none.

questions.q: You open the Fairfield site manager's Directory card and click Chat. Where does it take you?
questions.explanation: Greens talks on Teams and Nexus has no chat of its own. Chat, Call and Video open Teams.

questions.q: When does a borrowed pressure washer's due date start counting?
questions.explanation: The due date counts from the handover, when you take it or confirm receipt, not from when you asked.

questions.q: A note you have not shared cannot be opened by your manager.
questions.explanation: True. A note is private to you and the people you share it with. That is also why a problem written in a note reaches nobody.

questions.q: You missed two checkpoint questions in this course. How many quiz tries did that use?
questions.explanation: Checkpoints are practice and never count as a quiz try. They point you to what is worth rereading.

questions.q: You used all three tries on a final quiz. Who can unlock another round?
questions.explanation: Your manager (or the course owner) can unlock another round. Reread the listed lessons before you use it.

questions.q: A policy you signed last month gets a typo fix. Must you sign it again?
options: No; only a new version that changes the policy asks again
Yes; every edit needs a new signature
questions.explanation: A new version that changes the policy brings it back for your signature. A small fix like a typo does not.

questions.q: Your training plan's courses are due within how many days of your start date?
questions.explanation: New facility hires have 30 days from their start date to finish the plan. Due dates show on My Learning.

questions.q: It is your first day. Which of these is on the first-day list?
questions.explanation: Announcements reach the Dashboard only through their widget, so add it on day one. The others are optional preferences.

questions.q: You find a cracked fence post on your lot walk. Which habit applies?
options: A line in your End of Day
questions.explanation: Anything another person must act on is a ticket or a form, one problem each, with a photo. Notes and texts leave no tracked record.
